- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates 30d horizon; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply 5-day moving average to forecast to reduce noise.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 75.00 → 70.00), model often holds too long; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often ignores it; add 1–2% downward bias to 30d forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
